p.src: Now it is told that Li Jun, the River-Dragon, took advantage of the swollen waters after the heavy rain and, together with the two Zhang brothers and the three Ruan brothers, led the naval forces in separate parties. At the appointed hour, they breached the Zhibo Canal and diverted the Jin River to inundate the city of Taiyuan County. In an instant, the waters surged furiously. Suddenly the rushing waters came hurtling on, and in a moment great waves arose. Soldiers charged in aboard wooden rafts, while officers came flying over the deluge. Gods howled and ghosts wailed; the darkened sun shed no light; peaks shook and mountains crumbled, while the vast roar of the waves sounded like wrath. The city walls all collapsed, and every guard post was swept away. Banners vanished beneath the waves, amid a confusion of blue and red weapons and armor. The churning billows could not be stemmed, and white-crested waves thrust across one another. Corpses bobbed and sank like fish and turtles, while hot blood seethed together with the waves. In moments trees were torn up by the roots, and in an instant rafters and eaves went skimming over the water.

p.src: The city was then in utter turmoil. When soldiers and civilians saw the water suddenly arrive, they scrambled dripping wet onto walls and rooftops, climbed trees, and clung to beams; the old, the weak, and the stout could do no more than climb onto platforms and tables. In the blink of an eye, even the tables and stools floated away, houses collapsed, and all became fish and turtles in the flood. Outside the city, Li Jun, the two Zhang brothers, and the three Ruan brothers rode aboard the Flying River and Heaven-Floater and approached until they were level with the city walls. The soldiers clambered onto the walls, each wielding a sharp blade, and cut down the defenders. Other soldiers came charging on wooden rafts, and every section of wall they struck collapsed. Zhang Xiong was on the gate tower, crying out in despair, when Zhang Heng and Zhang Shun left the Flying River and mounted the wall. With broad-bladed sabers in hand, they gave a shout, rushed up the tower, and cut down more than ten soldiers in quick succession, sending the rest scrambling away for their lives. Before Zhang Xiong could dodge, Zhang Heng felled him with one sweep of his saber. Zhang Shun rushed forward and, with a single chop, struck off his head. By the time the floodwaters dispersed and receded, countless soldiers and civilians in the city had drowned or been crushed to death. Beams, pillars, doors, window lattices, household goods, and corpses drifted downstream and clogged the southern part of the city. Only the Summer Palace, built by Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi, stood upon high and solid foundations. Nearby soldiers and civilians all rushed up there, but in the crush and trampling more than two thousand people also died. Including those who survived on the high ground and atop the city walls, scarcely more than a thousand soldiers and civilians remained alive. The people outside the city, however, had been secretly warned by Vanguard Lu, who summoned the village heads and instructed them to make preparations in advance: at the sound of the gong, every resident was to climb immediately to high ground. Moreover, the country outside the city was open and spacious, allowing the water to drain away quickly; thus the people there escaped being submerged.

p.src: Li Jun, the River-Dragon, now led the naval forces in occupying the western gate; Zhang Heng, the Boatman, and Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, seized the northern gate; Ruan Xiaoer, the Ferocious Giant, and Ruan Xiaowu, the Short-Lived Second Son, occupied the eastern gate; and Ruan Xiaoqi, the Living King of Hell, took the southern gate. At all four gates, the banners of the Song army were raised. By evening the waters had receded and dry ground reappeared. Li Jun and the others threw open the city gates and invited Vanguard Lu and his army to enter. Not a cock crowed nor a dog barked within the city; corpses lay piled like mountains. Though Zhang Xiong and his fellows had amassed a full measure of wickedness, this stratagem of Li Jun's was far too cruel and deadly. The thousand-odd survivors knelt scattered about in the muddy water and kowtowed as ceaselessly as candles being planted, begging for their lives. Lu Junyi counted them and found only a dozen or so soldiers among the group; all the rest were common people. Xiang Zhong and Xu Yue had climbed into a great juniper tree beside a rear building of the commandery headquarters. When they saw the water recede, they slid down, only to be captured by the southern army and taken before Vanguard Lu. Lu Junyi ordered them beheaded and their heads displayed as a warning. He had silver from the county treasury distributed to relieve the flood-stricken people inside and outside the city; and sent men to report the victory to Vanguard Song. Meanwhile, he ordered the soldiers to bury the dead, rebuild the walls and houses, and summon the people back to live there.

p.src: We shall say no more of Lu Junyi pacifying the people and setting affairs in order in Taiyuan County, but return to the time before Taiyuan fell. Tian Hu, commanding an army of one hundred thousand, had encamped south of Mount Tongdi because of the rain. His scouts came to report that Imperial Kinsman Wu had died of illness and that the princess and her consort had immediately withdrawn their army to Xiangyuan to encoffin and mourn him. Tian Hu was greatly alarmed. He sent men into Xiangyuan to proclaim his decree, ordering Qiongying to guard the city and Quan Yu to come forward for service. He also demanded to know why none of the messengers previously dispatched to Xiangyuan had returned to report.

p.src: The next day the rain cleared. At first light, a mounted scout came racing in with an urgent report that Song Jiang had sent Sun An and Ma Ling at the head of troops to oppose them. When Tian Hu heard the report, he flew into a rage. “Sun An and Ma Ling both received high office and rich stipends from me. Their rebellion today cannot be tolerated by reason or justice. I shall go and question them myself. Exert yourselves, my lords! Whoever captures the pair shall receive a thousand pieces of gold and be made a marquis over ten thousand households.” Tian Hu then personally drove his army forward to confront the Song forces. When the northern army examined the Song banners, they discovered that the commanders were actually Sun Li, the Sickly Yuchi, and Ma Lin, the Iron-Flute Immortal. Before the northern ranks, golden maces stood thickly arrayed, iron axes were drawn up side by side, swords and halberds formed ordered lines, and banners marched in companies. Beneath a russet-yellow parasol embroidered with a nine-coiled flying dragon, mounted on a white horse with silver mane, jade bridle, and golden saddle, sat Tian Hu, the outlaw king. He rode before the ranks to supervise the battle in person. Behind the southern lines, Song Jiang arrived with the forces of Wu Yong, Sun Xin, Mistress Gu, Wang Ying, Hu Sanniang, Sun Li, Zhu Tong, and Yan Shun. Song Jiang likewise supervised the battle in person.

p.src: When Tian Hu heard that it was Song Jiang, he was just about to send a general into battle to capture him when a mounted messenger came galloping up and reported: “Guan Sheng and his men have taken the two cities of Yushe and Dagu in succession. On the western route, Lu Junyi's army has also captured the two counties of Pingyao and Jiexiu. They diverted water to flood the city of Taiyuan, leaving not a single soldier or officer alive within. Right Chancellor Bian Xiang had encamped at Mount Mian and was holding out against Hua Rong and the others, when Lu Junyi led his troops from Taiyuan and attacked him from the rear. Chancellor Bian could not withstand an attack from both sides and suffered a crushing defeat. Bian Xiang was captured alive by Lu Junyi and carried over to the enemy lines. Lu Junyi and Guan Sheng have now joined their armies and surrounded Qinyuan County as tightly as an iron barrel.” After hearing this, Tian Hu was so alarmed that he knew not what to do. He hurriedly issued an order to withdraw the army and retreat into Weisheng for defense.

p.src: At once Li Tianxi and the others held the battle line, while Xue Shi, Lin Xin, Hu Ying, and Tang Chang escorted Tian Hu away ahead of them. Suddenly, cannon fire thundered north of Mount Tongdi. Acting on Song Jiang's secret orders, Lu Zhishen, Liu Tang, Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun had led a force of picked infantry around to the mountain's northern side, and now came charging forward along two routes. Tian Hu hurriedly drove his Imperial Guard cavalry forward to meet them, only for Ma Ling and Sun An to lead another force in a slanting charge from the east. Ma Ling, with the two Wheels of Wind and Fire beneath his feet, hurled his golden brick wildly among the northern troops; Sun An hacked about him with his twin swords. Leading their troops, the two commanders burst into the northern ranks as though no one stood before them, splitting the army in two. Though the northern army numbered a hundred thousand, the three forces Wu Yong had deployed charged and wheeled through its ranks, slaughtering in every direction. The northern army was utterly defeated, scattered like falling stars and broken clouds, its formations torn to pieces. The false minister Li Tianxi and the others now guarded Tian Hu as they fought their way eastward in flight. But Lu Zhishen and his men, leading troops armed with javelins, round shields, and throwing knives, carved a bloody path through the enemy and came charging toward them; they again scattered the forces of Li Tianxi, Zheng Zhirui, Xue Shi, Lin Xin, and the others, sending them fleeing westward. Tian Hu's men were Imperial Guards, chosen from among the bravest and most skilled, yet although they had long fought the imperial army, they had never encountered foes so fierce. How could they possibly withstand them today?

p.src: Only Commander Hu Ying, Tang Chang, Chief Administrator Ye Qing, the Commandants of the Imperial Guard, and several other officers now remained at Tian Hu's side, escorting him in flight with five thousand battered survivors. Just as their peril was greatest, another body of troops suddenly swept in from the east. At the sight, Tian Hu raised his face to heaven and cried, “Heaven has destroyed me!” The northern troops looked toward the oncoming force. At its head rode a handsome young general, wearing a green kerchief and green battle robe, a pear-blossom spear in his hand and a tall, snow-white, curly-maned horse beneath him. The inscription on his banner was perfectly clear: “Prince-Consort Quan Yu, Vanguard of the Southern Pacification and Imperial Restoration.” Ye Qing, who was following close beside Tian Hu, saw the banner and reported it to him. Tian Hu issued an order that the prince-consort was to come quickly to his sovereign's rescue. Prince-Consort Quan approached, dismounted, and knelt to report: “Your servant addresses Your Majesty. Since I am clad in armor, I cannot prostrate myself fully. For this offense I deserve ten thousand deaths.” Tian Hu said, “You are pardoned; you have committed no offense.” Prince-Consort Quan reported again: “The situation is desperate. I beg Your Majesty to enter Xiangyuan and shelter there for the moment from the enemy's attack. Once the princess and I have driven back the Song troops, I shall invite Your Majesty to return to the inner palace at Weisheng, where we may devise a sound plan and restore your dominion.”

p.src: Tian Hu was overjoyed. He issued the command, and they set out at once for Xiangyuan. Prince-Consort Quan remained in the rear to hold off the pursuing troops and generals. Tian Hu and his party had already reached the walls of Xiangyuan when shouts of battle filled the sky behind them and the pursuers closed in. Seeing them, the officers and soldiers guarding Xiangyuan hurriedly opened the gates and lowered the drawbridge. Hu Ying led the troops in front. Hearing the pursuers behind them, the soldiers surged into the city in a single rush, no longer caring what became of their king. Hu Ying had only just passed through the gate when a wooden clapper sounded sharply. Ambush troops sprang out on both sides and drove Hu Ying and more than three thousand men into concealed pits, where soldiers stabbed them wildly with long spears. Pitifully, not one of those three thousand survived. From within the city came a great shout: “Take Tian Hu alive!” Seeing the upheaval within the city, Tian Hu realized only then that it was a trap. He urgently reined his horse around and fled north. Zhang Qing and Ye Qing spurred after him. Tian Hu's fine horse was swift, and they and their soldiers could not catch him; he had already drawn a bowshot ahead when a whirlwind suddenly rose before his mount. Within it appeared a woman, who cried aloud: “Villain Tian Hu! You brought ruin upon my husband and me. Where do you think you can flee today?” Beside the woman another ghostly gust arose and rolled straight into Tian Hu's face; then the woman silently vanished. Tian Hu's horse suddenly reared and neighed in terror, throwing him to the ground. Zhang Qing and Ye Qing caught up, leaped from their mounts, and rushed forward with the soldiers to seize him. Tang Chang led his men forward at a gallop, leveling his spear as he came to the rescue. Seeing Tang Chang bearing down on him, Zhang Qing hurriedly mounted, flicked a stone through the air, and struck Tang Chang squarely in the face, knocking him from his horse. Zhang Qing shouted, “I am no Quan Yu! I am Zhang Qing, the ‘Featherless Arrow,’ a commander under the Song vanguard of the Celestial Court.” At that moment Li Kui and Wu Song charged out of the city with five hundred infantrymen. With a great roar, the two men fell upon the Palace Marshal's generals, the Commandants of the Imperial Guard, and more than two thousand others, scattering them like falling stars and broken clouds. Zhang Qing speared Tang Chang to death, bound Tian Hu, and had him escorted into the city. Then the gates were closed, and they waited until Vanguard Song had driven off the northern army before sending the captive away. When Lu Zhishen arrived in pursuit, he saw that Tian Hu had already been captured and taken into the city. Lu Zhishen and the others turned westward again and fought their way to the flank of Mount Tongdi.

p.src: Qiongying, acting on Military Adviser Wu’s secret plan, had led Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Yue He, Duan Jingzhu, Wang Dingliu, Yu Baosi, Cai Fu, and Cai Qing, together with five thousand troops, all bearing the banners and insignia of the Northern Army, into ambush beside Mount Shipan outside Wuxiang County. When Qiongying and her companions learned that Tian Hu had joined battle with their forces, she led them on a swift march through the night to the walls of Weisheng. By the time they arrived, evening had fallen: the sunset glow had faded and the new moon hung like a hook. Beneath the walls, Qiongying called out in her sweet, warbling voice, “I am the Princess. I have escorted the King here. Open the gates at once!” The soldiers guarding the city immediately hurried to report this within the royal palace. On hearing the report, Tian Bao and Tian Biao mounted and raced to the southern wall. They hurried up the gate tower to look and indeed saw, beneath a russet-yellow parasol, the King seated on a white horse with a carved saddle and silver mane. Before him rode a woman general whose banner bore the great words “Princess Qiongying,” while ministers, commanders, and other officials followed at a distance. Qiongying called loudly, “Commander Hu and the others were defeated in battle by the Song forces, so I have personally escorted the King here. Have the officials come out of the city at once to receive His Majesty!” Seeing that it was Tian Hu, Tian Bao and the others ordered the gates opened at once and went out to receive him. The two men had only just reached the horse when the King upon it thundered, “Warriors, seize these two traitors for me!” The soldiers surged forward together and captured them. Tian Bao and Tian Biao cried, “We have committed no crime!” They tried desperately to struggle, but the soldiers had already bound them with ropes. This “Tian Hu” was in fact a soldier whom Wu Yong had ordered Sun An to select from the Southern Army because his features closely resembled Tian Hu’s; he had been dressed exactly like him. The ministers and commanders behind him were likewise Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, and several others in disguise. At once they all drew their weapons. Wang Dingliu, Yu Baosi, Cai Fu, and Cai Qing took more than five hundred men and escorted Tian Bao and Tian Biao through the night to Xiangyuan. Those upon the walls saw Tian Bao and Tian Biao seized and then marched southward, and realized that it was a trick. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao fought at Qiongying’s side. Outside the walls, Yue He and Duan Jingzhu hastily ordered the soldiers to cast off their Northern Army disguises, revealing the uniforms of the Southern Army beneath. All charged into the city together and seized the southern gate. Brandishing their broad-bladed swords, Yue He and Duan Jingzhu led the troops onto the walls, scattered the defenders, and raised the banners of the Song army. Just then Zhang Qing arrived with more than eight thousand men and drove his troops into the city. p.src: They were just about to lead their troops out of the city when, as Heaven itself abhorred the wickedness of the rebels, Lu Junyi arrived after capturing Qinyuan, leading a great army. On seeing the banners at the southern gate, he hurried his forces into the city, joined troops with Zhang Qing, and pursued and slaughtered the Northern Army. Qin Ming, Yang Zhi, Du Qian, and Song Wan led troops to seize the eastern gate. Ou Peng, Deng Fei, Lei Heng, and Yang Lin seized the western gate. Huang Xin, Chen Da, Yang Chun, and Zhou Tong led troops to seize the northern gate. Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, Jiao Ting, Mu Chun, Zheng Tianshou, Zou Yuan, and Zou Run led infantrymen wielding great swords and broad axes and hacked their way into the front of the royal palace; Gong Wang, Ding Desun, Li Li, Shi Yong, Tao Zongwang led infantry through the rear service gate, cutting their way inside. Countless consorts, concubines, eunuchs, and other attendants within the palace were killed. On hearing of the upheaval, Tian Ding cut his own throat and died. Zhang Qing, Qiongying, Zhang Qing the Gardener, Sun Erniang, Tang Bin, Wen Zhongrong, Cui Ye, Geng Gong, Cao Zheng, Xue Yong, Li Zhong, Zhu Fu, Shi Qian, and Bai Sheng split up to kill the false ministers, false palace commanders, false privy councillors and all those beneath them, along with the rebel royal clan and imperial relatives who had received false titles. Truly: Beneath the golden stairs of the hall, heads rolled; before the jade-paved court gate, hot blood sprayed. Say not that jade and stone alike were indiscriminately destroyed; whether they met blessing or disaster, let each search his own heart.

p.src: The Song troops then slaughtered their way through Weisheng until corpses lay across the streets and blood filled the drains. Lu Junyi issued an order forbidding any harm to the common people. He quickly dispatched men ahead to report the victory to Vanguard Song. The turmoil caused by the Song troops continued that night until the fifth watch before finally subsiding, and great numbers of officers and soldiers surrendered.

p.src: At daybreak, Lu Junyi mustered and counted his officers. Apart from Zhu Wu, the “Resourceful Strategist,” who had remained to guard Qinyuan, none of the other commanders had suffered injury or loss. Only the surrendered general Geng Gong had been trampled to death by men and horses. All the commanders came forward to present their achievements. Jiao Ting brought in Tian Ding’s corpse slung over a pack animal. Grinding her teeth in hatred, Qiongying drew her sword, cut off his head, and dismembered the body. By this time, Lady Ni, wife of Wu Li, was already dead. Qiongying sought out Lady An, wife of Ye Qing, then took leave of Lu Junyi and went with Zhang Qing to Xiangyuan to escort Tian Hu and the others to Vanguard Song. While Lu Junyi was attending to military affairs, a scout suddenly arrived with the report that the northern general Fang Xuedu had surrounded Suo Chao and Tang Long in Yushe County. Lu Junyi immediately ordered Guan Sheng, Qin Ming, Lei Heng, Chen Da, Yang Chun, Yang Lin, and Zhou Tong to lead troops to the rescue of Suo Chao and the others.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang defeated Li Tianxi and the others at Mount Tongdi. He sent men to report to Pacification Commissioner Chen: “The rebels’ lair has been taken and their leader captured. We request that Your Excellency come to Weisheng to settle affairs.” Song Jiang led the main army to the outskirts of Weisheng, where Lu Junyi and the others received him and escorted him into the city. Song Jiang posted proclamations to reassure the people. Lu Junyi had Bian Xiang brought before him under guard. Seeing that Bian Xiang was imposing in stature and appearance, Song Jiang personally untied his bonds and treated him with courtesy. Moved by Song Jiang’s generosity and spirit, Bian Xiang gratefully surrendered and pledged his allegiance.

p.src: The next day, Zhang Qing, Qiongying, and Ye Qing arrived, bringing Tian Hu, Tian Bao, and Tian Biao as prisoners in cage-carts. Qiongying and Zhang Qing went together to pay their respects to her uncle, Vanguard Song. Qiongying thanked Wang Ying and the others for pardoning her former offenses against them. Song Jiang had Tian Hu and the others confined separately, intending to escort them all to the Eastern Capital and present them as captives when the army returned in triumph. He then ordered a banquet prepared to celebrate Zhang Qing and Qiongying. That same day, Fang Shun and the other officers defending Wuxiang, a county under Weisheng, came to surrender the registers of the soldiers and civilian households, together with the money and grain in the granaries and treasuries. After rewarding them, Song Jiang ordered Fang Shun to remain in command of the defenses as before. After Song Jiang had spent two days in Weisheng, a scout reported that Guan Sheng and his men had reached Yushe County and, joining with Suo Chao and Tang Long in an attack from within and without, had slain the northern commander Fang Xuedu. More than five thousand northern soldiers were killed, and all the rest surrendered. Song Jiang was overjoyed and told his commanders, “It is entirely through the efforts of all my brothers that we have succeeded in pacifying the rebels.” He immediately recorded in detail the merits of every commander, as well as the great service rendered by Zhang Qing and Qiongying in capturing the rebel chiefs and destroying their lair.

p.src: Chen Guan and Song Jiang ordered that, of all the captured rebels and holders of spurious offices, Tian Hu, Tian Bao, and Tian Biao alone were to be kept for separate transport to the Eastern Capital; all the rest who had followed the rebels were beheaded at the execution ground in Weisheng. The places not yet recovered were the prefectures and counties of Pu, Jie, and others under Jinning. When the rebel functionaries and corrupt officials learned that Tian Hu had been captured, half fled and scattered, while the other half came forward to surrender. Pacification Commissioner Chen accepted every surrender and restored them to the status of lawful commoners. He had proclamations posted throughout the region offering amnesty and pacification, so that the people might live in peace. The remaining followers of the rebels who had harmed no one were likewise permitted to surrender voluntarily, return to village life, and recover their property and farmland. Once the prefectures and counties had been recovered, officers and troops were assigned to each for defense, to protect the borders and bring peace to the people. Of this no more need be said.
